rule: Add codes when needed. Never rename or reuse a code: old releases must stay comparable.

categories.label: Requirements incomplete or ambiguous
categories.definition: The requirement or acceptance criteria did not state, or stated unclearly, the behaviour UAT expected.

categories.label: Test coverage gap
categories.definition: The requirement was clear and the build was wrong; no developer-side test exercised the failing path.

categories.label: Environment or configuration
categories.definition: Works as built, fails because of environment, deployment or configuration differences.

categories.label: Integration or interface
categories.definition: A contract, payload, sequence or timing problem between two systems or modules.

categories.label: Data validation
categories.definition: Missing or wrong validation, defaulting or handling of data values.

categories.label: UI or UX
categories.definition: Layout, labels, navigation or interaction is wrong while the underlying logic is right.

categories.label: Performance
categories.definition: Correct result, unacceptable time or resource use.

categories.label: Regression from a previous fix
categories.definition: Previously working behaviour broken by a later change. Needs evidence of the earlier working state.

categories.label: Process or workflow
categories.definition: The software matches its design; the delivery or business process around it caused the bug report.

categories.label: Other
categories.definition: None of the above. Say why in root_cause.

escape_reasons.definition: Developer data did not include the case UAT used.
The local or dev environment differs from UAT in a way that hid the defect.
The other system was mocked, stubbed or absent before UAT.
Developer and tester read the acceptance criteria differently.
The path could have been tested locally and no test existed.
A test existed and was skipped, disabled or not run for this change.

catch_levels.definition: An in-process unit test could have caught it.
An API or contract test against a running service could have caught it.
A test with the real or simulated neighbouring system could have caught it.
An automated end-to-end UI test could have caught it.
Only a manual check before UAT could have caught it.
Realistically visible only in UAT: business judgment or production-like data.
